question: A trader marks his goods 40% above the cost price and gives a discount of 25%. If he gains Rs. 75 on an item, what is the cost price of the item?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100x. Since markup is 40%, Marked Price (MP) = 140x.

Selling Price (SP) after 25% discount on MP = 140x × 0.75 = 105x.

Profit = SP − CP = 105x − 100x = 5x.

Given 5x = Rs. 75 ⇒ x = 15.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup % = 40%

Discount % = 25%

Profit = Rs. 75

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (100 + Markup %) ÷ 100

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount %) ÷ 100

 

 

 Markup: +40%

 

 

 Discount: -25%

 
 CP = 100x

 
 SP = 105x

 
 MP = 140x

 

 

 Profit: +5x

 Profit (5x) = Rs. 75 ⇒ x = 15

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100x.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100x + (40 ÷ 100) × 100x = 140x

⇒ Discount given on MP = 25% of 140x = 35x

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount = 140x − 35x = 105x

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 105x − 100x = 5x

⇒ We are given that Profit = Rs. 75

⇒ 5x = 75

⇒ x = 15

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = 100 × 15 = Rs. 1500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), never on the Cost Price. The formula for actual SP is: SP = MP × (1 − Discount / 100).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the equivalent single discount percentage is given by: (a + b − a × b ÷ 100)%.

Direct Relation between CP and MP

A very useful trick for quick calculations: The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is exactly CP / MP = (100 − Discount %) / (100 + Profit %).
